info.title: ShadouCMDB API
info.description:
REST API for ShadouCMDB. This API is the only database client; the web UI uses nothing else.

- Collections are paginated with `limit`/`offset` and return `{ data, page: { limit, offset, total } }`.
- `sort=field` ascending, `sort=-field` descending. `q` searches. Filters that take ids accept comma-separated lists.
- Every error uses the `ErrorEnvelope` shape; invalid input is always 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` with per-field `details`.
- Sign in with `POST /api/v1/auth/login`; the session travels in the `shadoucmdb_session` cookie. Every operation except the health probes, login and first-run setup answers 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` without a live session.
- POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE also need the `X-CSRF-Token` header (the `csrfToken` from login or `/api/v1/auth/me`, also in the `shadoucmdb_csrf` cookie); without it: 403 `CSRF_TOKEN_INVALID`.
- Permissions come from the permission profiles a user holds. A missing global permission (named in each operation's description) or class permission (view/create/edit/delete) answers 403 `FORBIDDEN`. Lists only contain CIs of classes the user may view.
- Writes are recorded in the audit log (`/api/v1/audit-log`) with the signed-in user as the actor.
- Send `X-Request-Id` to correlate a request; it is echoed back and stored with audit rows.

get.summary: Liveness: the process is up (does not touch the database)
Readiness: database reachable and all migrations applied
get.description: Returns 200 with status "ready" only when the database answers and every migration in this build is applied; otherwise 503 with the same body shape.

503.description: Not ready: database unreachable or migrations pending

get.summary: Whether first-run setup is needed (no users exist yet)

post.summary: Create the first administrator and sign them in (only while no users exist)
post.description: The new user holds the built-in Administrator profile. 409 once any user exists. Sets the session and CSRF cookies. `shadoucmdb create-admin` does the same from the command line.

400.description: Invalid input (code VALIDATION_ERROR) with per-field details

409.description: Conflict: CONFLICT (duplicate or not allowed in this state), IN_USE, VERSION_CONFLICT or LAST_ADMINISTRATOR

post.summary: Sign in with username and password
post.description: Sets the `shadoucmdb_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure behind HTTPS) and the `shadoucmdb_csrf` cookie. 401 for a wrong username or password. After 5 failures for a username, each further failure locks it for 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, ... up to 15 min; while locked the answer is 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After. Once 300 failures in 10 min for all usernames together are reached, sign-in is slowed rather than refused: attempts queue and go through one per 2 s (a correct password still signs in); only when 64 are already queued is the next one answered 429.

401.description: Not signed in, session expired, or wrong credentials (code UNAUTHENTICATED)

429.description: Too many failed password attempts (code RATE_LIMITED); see the Retry-After header

post.summary: Sign out: end this session and clear its cookies

get.summary: Relationship graph around a CI in one call (nodes + edges)
get.description: Breadth-first traversal of live relationships up to `depth` hops. For a Server -> Application -> Database view, ask from the application with `direction=outgoing`, or from the server with `direction=both&depth=2`. Needs view on the root's class; CIs of classes the caller may not view are left out (and not traversed).

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: outgoing follows source->target (app -> runs_on -> server); incoming the reverse; symmetric types are always followed

parameters.name: maxNodes
parameters.description: Stop expanding once this many CIs are collected

get.summary: Global search across CIs, ranked, with the fields that matched
get.description: Matches name, hostname and serial number (substring), IP address (prefix, or containment when `q` is an IP or CIDR), notes (word prefix) and attribute values (text/enum substring, IP/CIDR prefix). Exact matches rank first, then name prefix, then trigram similarity. Only CIs in classes the caller may view.

get.description: Requires `config.export_import`. Data model (classes, attributes, relationship types and rules), lookups (statuses, environments, locations, owners, lookup lists), permission profiles (not the built-in one) and UI settings including the logo and favicon. Never contains users, passwords, sessions, CIs or relationships. Everything refers to everything else by key, so the file imports into another install. Answers with `Content-Disposition: attachment`.

post.summary: Import a configuration file (dry run or apply)
post.description: Requires `config.export_import`. `mode=dry_run` validates the file and runs the whole import in a transaction that is rolled back, returning the diff; `mode=apply` does the same and commits. Rows are matched by key (owners by kind and name, profiles by name) and created or updated; nothing is deleted, so data missing from the file is kept (counted as `notInFile`). The `uiSettings` section replaces the settings (as a new version) and the logo and favicon. All sections are optional. Problems in the file are reported together as 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with paths into the file; a change the data model does not allow (e.g. making an attribute required while CIs lack a value) fails with the same error the admin API gives, with the file path prefixed. Profiles cannot grant more than the importing user holds (403). Every applied change is audited.

referenceClassId.description: When dataType is "reference": the class (or ancestor) the referenced CI must belong to

lookupListId.description: When dataType is "lookup": the admin-defined list its values come from

groupName.description: Form section the field is shown in, e.g. "Hardware"

helpText.description: Shown under the field on CI forms

defaultValue.description: Pre-filled on new CIs and stored when a CI is created without a value (same shape as the value)

isActive.description: Retired attributes keep their stored values but accept no new ones

inherited.description: Defined on an ancestor class rather than this one

EffectiveAttributeList.description: All attributes a CI of this class can carry (not paginated; bounded by the class lineage)

EffectivePermissions.description: What the signed-in user may do (the union of their profiles).

administrator.description: Holds the built-in Administrator profile (everything below is then all-true)

items.description: Rights that are not tied to a CI class.

classes.description: Rights on individual classes, beyond allClasses

FieldChange.description: One changed field: API names, values as in the file format (keys, not ids)

section.description: e.g. classes, attributes, lookupListValues, permissionProfiles, uiSettings

key.description: The row's key in the file (class.key for attributes, list.value for list values, kind:name for owners)

applied.description: True only for mode=apply (a dry run never changes anything)

changes.description: Every create, update and delete (unchanged rows are only counted)

uiSettingsIssues.description: References in the imported UI settings that do not resolve after the import (see GET /api/v1/ui-settings)

Issue.description: A reference the effective settings ignore, or a setting worth a second look

path.description: Path in the stored document, e.g. "listViews.2.columns.3"

parentId.description: Parent location (region > site > building > floor > room > rack)

isActive.description: Retired values stay on the CIs that hold them but cannot be chosen again

LookupRef.description: Compact reference to a lookup row

items.description: Owners have no key; they are matched by kind and name (case-insensitive)
An admin-defined lookup list with its values

externalRef.description: Identifier in an external directory (LDAP DN, IdP subject, HR id)

isBuiltin.description: The Administrator profile: every permission, read-only, cannot be deleted

items.description: Rights that are not tied to a CI class.

PublicBranding.description: Branding for the login page (no sign-in needed)

defaultTheme.description: Theme for users who have not picked one

applied.description: Absent when the database is unreachable

deletedAt.description: Set when the relationship was removed (soft delete)

version.description: Optimistic-locking counter; send it back in PATCH to detect concurrent edits

deletedAt.description: Set when the CI was deleted (soft delete); history keeps resolving

truncated.description: true when maxNodes stopped the expansion early

sourceClassId.description: Matches this class and all its descendants

targetClassId.description: Matches this class and all its descendants

isDirectional.description: false for symmetric types such as connected_to

SectionSummary.description: Counts for one section of the file

notInFile.description: Rows of this kind that exist here but are not in the file (kept as they are)

Session.description: The signed-in user, their permissions and the CSRF token to send back.

csrfToken.description:
Send as the X-CSRF-Token header on every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE
(also readable from the shadoucmdb_csrf cookie)

setupRequired.description: True while no user exists: the UI shows the first-run screen

allOf.description: How many of those rows already exist (matched by key)

attributeCount.description: Attributes defined directly on the class

StarterTemplateList.description: Every starter template (not paginated: they ship with the server)

allOf.description: Rows added by this install (each has an audit entry)
Rows that already existed and were left as they are

skipped.description: Rows not installed because they would clash with the current data model

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the file (also its ETag)

url.description: Where to load it from; the `v` parameter changes with the content, so it can be cached

UiAssets.description: Logo and favicon (null when not uploaded)

UiBranding.description: App name, colours and the default theme. Logo and favicon are uploaded separately (`/api/v1/ui-settings/assets/{kind}`).

appName.description: Shown in the header, the login page and the browser title; null means "ShadouCMDB"

primaryColor.description: Hex colour, e.g. "#1f6feb"; null keeps the built-in theme colour

accentColor.description: Hex colour, e.g. "#1f6feb"; null keeps the built-in theme colour

defaultTheme.description: Theme for users who have not picked one; system follows the operating system

UiClassLayout.description:
Detail page and form layout of one class. Fields not placed in a panel
follow in a trailing panel, grouped by attribute group as before.

hiddenFields.description: Fields not shown on the detail page or the form (name cannot be hidden)

readOnlyFields.description: Fields shown but not editable on the form (name cannot be read-only)

UiDashboard.description: Dashboard widgets in display order; null keeps the built-in dashboard

UiLayoutPanel.description: A panel (card) on the detail page and the form

fields.description: Fields in display order (built-in fields or attributes.<key>)

collapsed.description: Start collapsed on the detail page

UiListSort.description: Sort for an inventory list; `field` is one of the inventory sort fields

UiListView.description: The inventory list of one class

columns.description: Columns in display order: built-in fields (name, class, status, environment, owner, location, hostname, ipAddress, serialNumber, notes, createdAt, updatedAt) or attributes.<key>

UiNavClassItem.description: A class inside a navigation section

label.description: Display label; null keeps the default

UiNavEntry.description:
One menu entry. `type` decides which other fields apply: page -> `page`;
class -> `classKey`; section -> `key`, `label` and `items`.

page.description: Built-in pages of the web UI

label.description: Display label; null keeps the default

items.description: section: its classes in display order

UiNavigation.description:
Menu order, labels, hidden entries and class sections. Pages and classes
that are not listed appear after the listed ones, in their default order.

oneOf.description: Sort for an inventory list; `field` is one of the inventory sort fields

UiSettings.description: The current UI settings as the web UI applies them

version.description: Send it back in PUT; it changes with every save

updatedBy.description: Username of whoever saved this version

settings.description: The effective settings: references to classes, attributes and lookups that do not exist are left out (see `issues`)

issues.description: What the effective settings ignore or flag, with paths into the stored document

UiSettingsDocument.description: Every UI setting. All sections are optional; `{}` is the default UI.

UiSettingsSection.description:
The UI settings document with the logo and favicon. Importing it replaces
the current settings (as a new version) and the images: a null logo or
favicon removes the current one.

UiSettingsVersion.description: A saved version with its document as stored

title.description: Display label; null keeps the default

search.description: saved_search: the search (required for that type)

UsageCount.description: How many records of one kind refer to the row.

blocking.description: A non-zero count prevents deleting the row; retire it with isActive=false instead

UsageReport.description: What still refers to a record, so the UI can warn before a destructive change

inUse.description: True when a blocking count is non-zero: DELETE would return 409 IN_USE

username.description: Sign-in name, unique regardless of case

isActive.description: Disabled users cannot sign in and their sessions end

csrfHeader.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfHeader.description: The session's csrfToken; required on POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE

sessionCookie.name: shadoucmdb_session
sessionCookie.description: Session cookie set by POST /api/v1/auth/login (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax)

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness and readiness probes for orchestrators and load balancers.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: First-run setup, sign-in with a local username and password, sign-out, and the current user's permissions.

tags.name: Configuration items
tags.description: CIs: the tracked assets. Includes the relationship graph around a CI.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Global search across CIs and their attribute values.

tags.name: Relationships
tags.description: Typed, directional edges between CIs. Removal is a soft delete.

tags.name: CI classes
tags.description: CI types in an inheritance tree. Adding a class is data entry, not a migration. Changing the data model needs datamodel.manage.

tags.name: Attribute definitions
tags.description: Typed custom fields per class, inherited by subclasses.

tags.name: Relationship types
tags.description: Relationship types (runs_on, depends_on, ...) and the rules for which classes they may connect.

tags.name: Owners
tags.description: People and teams accountable for CIs.

tags.name: Lookup lists
tags.description: Lists an administrator defines (e.g. "Support contract") whose values "lookup" attributes store.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: Administration: starter data models (classes, attributes, relationship rules and lookups) installed on a bare database.

tags.name: UI settings
tags.description: Branding, navigation, dashboard, list views and detail/form layouts for every user: one versioned, audited document plus the logo and favicon. Reading needs a session (branding and images are public for the login page); changing needs customization.manage.

tags.name: Audit log
tags.description: Read-only change history written in the same transaction as every change.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Administration: local user accounts, passwords and the permission profiles they hold.

tags.name: Permission profiles
tags.description: Administration: named sets of global and per-CI-class permissions. Users can hold several; the built-in Administrator profile holds everything.

tags.name: Configuration export/import
tags.description: Administration: the whole configuration (data model, lookups, permission profiles, UI settings) as one JSON file, and importing such a file with a dry-run diff first. Needs config.export_import.
